learning_outcomes.text: Represent different types of information for processing by digital computers

Name the elements of an instruction set architecture, based on data-processing-appropriate representation of information and the principles of instruction-based execution of processing instructions, and assess their effects on programming
Explain the interaction of hardware and software
Formulate basic elements of procedural programming in a machine language
Assess the effect of programming alternatives on execution speed
Explain concepts for performance enhancement in modern processors and associated problems
Independently create and execute small assembler programs

syllabus_topics: Classification of computer architectures and computer description
Information representation in the computer: Polyadic number systems, conversion methods, complement representations, floating-point representations
Instruction set architectures: Classification, programming model, IA32 instruction set as example, machine-oriented programming concepts (addressing modes, subroutine techniques, others)
von Neumann computer: Mode of operation and structure, control unit, arithmetic logic unit, memory unit and memory technologies, I/O units, bus system
Advanced concepts in current computer architectures (Cache, multi-core architectures, pipelining, superscalar)
Tasks for assembler programming with NASM (x86/IA32/Intel 64-Assembler)
assessment_rules: Successful completion of the practical work (3.2) is a prerequisite for participation in the written examination (3.1). Within the practical work, several testates must be acquired. For successful completion of the tasks, a testate is awarded by the lecturer. A minimum of 80% of the testates, covering essential topics of the lecture, must be completed.
